mainTopic: How the משנה's rule about חליפין applies to goods and coins, the views of רב ששת, רב נחמן and ריש לקיש, and why invalid coins can be traded
overview: The גמרא settles on a reading of the משנה: anything whose value must be estimated against another item, which leaves out a coin, can make a binding חליפין. It supports this with the משנה's example of swapping animals. It then shows how the earlier coin reading could explain that example. That explanation fits רב ששת, who holds that goods make חליפין. For רב נחמן, who holds that goods do not make חליפין, the example means money owed that is paid off with an animal. רב נחמן can say this because he follows רבי יוחנן: by Torah law money acquires, and the חכמים did not extend their משיכה decree to rare cases. ריש לקיש holds that משיכה comes from the Torah, so he is forced to explain the משנה like רב ששת. Next, ריש לקיש's statement that a pouch of coins can be traded for a pouch of coins is explained by רב אחא as referring to coins that are no longer valid money, and the גמרא explains why both kinds of invalid coin had to be mentioned. The amud ends by opening a new teaching from רבה in the name of רב הונא about selling 'for these coins.'

steps.title: The new reading of the משנה: anything that is valued against another item
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the משנה to mean that any item whose worth must be appraised against another item can create a binding exchange. Once one side takes his item, the other side is bound.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anything that gets appraised as payment for another item: as soon as one side acquires, the other side becomes obligated for the item given in exchange.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its reading of the משנה's line about goods acquiring one another. The משנה means items that need to be appraised, so it is not talking about a coin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A coin has a fixed, known value, so it is not 'appraised against another item.' By saying 'כל הנישום,' the משנה is telling us that all kinds of goods, not just a כלי, can make a חליפין deal. Once one person pulls his item into his possession, the deal is closed, and the other person carries the risk of the item he is getting.

keyTerms.meaning: That which is appraised (its value has to be estimated)
An exchange or barter that creates a קנין

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two ideas. 'Appraised against another item' is the way the גמרא leaves out a coin, because a coin's value is already known and does not need to be appraised.

phrases.english: Anything that is appraised as value for another item,
once this one acquires,
this one becomes obligated for the item exchanged.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion by giving the final reading of the משנה's clause.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה might have been teaching that a coin can make חליפין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה teaches that all appraised goods, not coins, can make חליפין.

steps.title: Support from the משנה's example of swapping animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the new reading. The משנה's own example ('How so? He swapped an ox for a cow') uses animals, not coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense, because the end of the משנה says: 'How so? He swapped an ox for a cow, or a donkey for an ox.' Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof for its reading from the next line of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'כיצד' (how so?) introduces an explanation of the line before it. Since the example is a swap of animals, which are goods, the line before it must also be about goods and not coins.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable, it makes sense
The latter part of the משנה
Learn from it (a proof is accepted)

phrases.english: So too it is reasonable,
since the latter clause teaches: How so?
If he exchanged an ox for a cow
or a donkey for an ox.
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for the reading given in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the משנה is talking about goods, not coins.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה: 'כיצד? החליף שור בפרה או חמור בשור.'
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's 'כיצד' example uses animals. That supports reading the whole rule as being about goods, not coins.

steps.title: How did the original coin reading explain 'how so'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to its first assumption, that the משנה meant a coin, and asks how that view would explain the animal example.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to what we first thought, that the משנה was talking about a coin, what does 'how so' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the earlier view, that coins make חליפין, would explain the משנה's animal example. This sets up an answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the line before was about coins, an example about animals does not seem to explain it. The גמרא wants to see whether the first reading had a way to deal with this. That would weaken the proof from step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: What entered his mind (what we assumed)

phrases.english: And according to what entered our mind at first,
a coin, what is the meaning of "how so"?
phrases.notes: This refers back to the earlier assumption that a coin can make a חליפין deal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the proof of step 2 against the earlier coin reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the coin reading would explain the animal example of 'כיצד'.

steps.title: The coin reading explained: goods also work
steps.stepSummary: Under the coin reading, the משנה adds that goods also make חליפין, and 'כיצד' explains that added point with the animal swap.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: goods also make חליפין. How so? He swapped an ox for a cow, or a donkey for an ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how the first view read the משנה. 'כיצד' explains an extra point that the משנה adds, that goods work too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this answer, the animal example no longer has to explain the coin rule. It explains an added idea, that goods ('פירי') also make חליפין. So the proof in step 2 is not decisive.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
and produce also effects exchange,
phrases.notes: 'פירי' here means ordinary goods, as opposed to a כלי. The 'also' means in addition to a coin.

phrases.english: How so? He exchanged an ox for a cow
or a donkey for an ox.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר, וּפֵירֵי נָמֵי עָבְדִי חֲלִיפִין
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה adds that goods also make חליפין, and 'כיצד' illustrates that added point.

steps.title: That answer works for רב ששת but not for רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 4. It fits רב ששת, who holds that goods make חליפין, but רב נחמן holds that only a כלי does, so how would he explain 'כיצד'?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רב ששת, who said goods make חליפין. But according to רב נחמן, who said a כלי does and goods do not, what does 'how so' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 4. That answer depends on goods working for חליפין, which רב נחמן does not accept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said the משנה adds that goods work too. רב נחמן holds that only a כלי can make חליפין, so for him the animal swap cannot be explaining a rule about goods. The coin reading now seems to have no explanation for 'כיצד' according to רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: אמורא who holds that goods can make חליפין
אמורא who holds that only a כלי can make חליפין

phrases.english: This works out well according to Rav Sheshet,
who said produce effects exchange,
but according to Rav Nachman, who said:
A vessel, yes,
but produce does not effect exchange,
what is the meaning of "how so"?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת, דְּאָמַר פֵּירֵי עָבְדִי חֲלִיפִין, אֶלָּא לְרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of step 4, that 'כיצד' illustrates goods also making חליפין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן holds that goods cannot make חליפין, so according to him the animal example cannot be illustrating that goods work.
steps.whyThisMatters: This forces the גמרא to find a different way for רב נחמן to read 'כיצד', which leads to his idea of money that works like חליפין (step 6).

steps.title: רב נחמן reads the example as money turned into an animal
steps.stepSummary: According to רב נחמן, the משנה means that sometimes money works like חליפין. An example is when someone owes money for an ox and gives a cow instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: there is money that works like an exchange. How so? He exchanged the money owed for an ox for a cow, or the money owed for a donkey for an ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 5 by explaining how רב נחמן would read 'כיצד' in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן cannot say the example shows goods making חליפין, so he reads it differently. A buyer took an ox and now owes money for it. He then gives the seller a cow in place of the money, and the cow is acquired just by settling the debt, the way חליפין works.

keyTerms.meaning: Money, or the price of something
There is money that works like an exchange
The money owed for an ox

steps.confusionAlert: The cow is not swapped for the ox itself. It is given in place of the money still owed for the ox.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
There is money that is like an exchange.
How so?
He exchanged the money owed for an ox for a cow,
or the money owed for a donkey for an ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 5 for רב נחמן
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'כיצד' must show goods making חליפין, which רב נחמן rejects
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כיצד' shows money owed being settled with an animal, which works like חליפין

steps.title: Why does רב נחמן allow money to work here
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רב נחמן's reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking what reason stands behind רב נחמן's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally money alone does not buy movable things; you need משיכה. So it is surprising that the cow is acquired just by settling a money debt, and the גמרא wants to know why רב נחמן allows it.

phrases.english: What is the reason of רב נחמן?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the answer of step 6
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How money can effectively acquire the cow when the rule is that money does not acquire movables

steps.title: רב נחמן follows רבי יוחנן: by Torah law money buys
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן holds like רבי יוחנן. By Torah law money buys things, and the חכמים required משיכה only out of worry that the seller will not protect goods that are already paid for.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי יוחנן, who says: by Torah law money acquires. Why did the חכמים say that pulling acquires? It is a decree, so the seller will not say to the buyer, 'Your wheat burned in the attic.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by explaining that רב נחמן follows רבי יוחנן's view about money and משיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the Torah, paying money is enough to buy an item. The חכמים added the need for משיכה because once a seller has the money, he might not bother to save the buyer's goods from a fire. So the item stays in the seller's hands and under his responsibility until it is pulled.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulling the item, a way of acquiring movables
A protective rule made by the חכמים

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the need for משיכה is a rule of the חכמים according to רבי יוחנן. That opens the door for the חכמים to leave some cases out of it.

phrases.english: He holds like רבי יוחנן.
Who said: by Torah law, money acquires.
And why did they say that pulling acquires?
It is a decree, in case the seller says to him:
Your wheat was burned in the attic.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב נחמן follows רבי יוחנן: by Torah law money acquires, and משיכה is only a rule of the חכמים

steps.title: The חכמים' decree does not cover rare cases
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים made their rule only for things that happen often. Paying off a money debt with an animal is rare, so money still works there.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a common matter the חכמים made a decree. For an uncommon matter the חכמים did not make a decree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining רב נחמן: the case in the משנה is rare, so the חכמים' rule requiring משיכה does not apply to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is unusual for a seller to agree to take an animal in place of the money he is owed. Because the case is rare, the חכמים did not include it in their rule, and the Torah law that money acquires stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: A common matter, something that happens often
The חכמים did not make a decree about it

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן: by Torah law money acquires (רבי יוחנן). The חכמים required משיכה only for common cases. Turning money owed into an animal is rare, so money alone works there, and that is 'money that is like חליפין.'

phrases.english: And for a common matter,
the חכמים made a decree about it.
For an uncommon matter,
phrases.notes: This is the case in the משנה: giving an animal in place of money owed hardly ever happens.

phrases.english: the חכמים did not make a decree about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of step 8 by explaining why the decree does not cover the משנה's case
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The decree requiring משיכה applies only to common cases, and the משנה's case is rare

steps.title: How would ריש לקיש explain the משנה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש holds that משיכה comes from the Torah itself. If he agrees with רב ששת, he can explain the משנה like רב ששת. The גמרא is setting up the problem of what to do if he agrees with רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to ריש לקיש, who says משיכה is stated outright in the Torah: this works if he holds like רב ששת, since he can explain the משנה like רב ששת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about ריש לקיש. It is setting up a challenge for the case where he holds like רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's answer depended on רבי יוחנן, who holds that money acquires by Torah law. ריש לקיש says that by Torah law only משיכה acquires, so money can never acquire, not even in a rare case. If ריש לקיש holds like רב ששת, there is no problem, because goods make חליפין and 'כיצד' simply shows that.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (usually followed by 'but what about...')

steps.confusionAlert: This line is only the first half of the question. The real difficulty, what ריש לקיש would say if he holds like רב נחמן, comes next.

phrases.english: And according to ריש לקיש,
who said that pulling is stated outright in the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: הָנִיחָא אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת,
phrases.english: this works out well if he holds like רב ששת,
he can explain it like רב ששת.
phrases.notes: That is the answer from step 4: goods make חליפין, and 'כיצד' shows the animal swap.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ דְּאָמַר מְשִׁיכָה מְפוֹרֶשֶׁת מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests whether the reading of steps 6 to 9 can work for ריש לקיש, who disagrees with רבי יוחנן
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's reading of 'כיצד', which depends on רבי יוחנן's view that money acquires by Torah law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under ריש לקיש, money cannot acquire movables by Torah law, so the 'rare case' answer fails. Only the רב ששת reading still works, which leaves a problem if ריש לקיש holds like רב נחמן.

steps.title: If ריש לקיש agrees with רב נחמן, how can he explain the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the question that started in step 10. If ריש לקיש agrees with רב נחמן's rules, he cannot use רב נחמן's way of explaining the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if ריש לקיש agrees with רב נחמן, who says that produce cannot be used for חליפין and a coin does not acquire, how would he explain the משנה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the problem it began in step 10. It asks how ריש לקיש could explain the משנה if he holds the same rules as רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן explained the משנה by saying money works by Torah law and the חכמים did not block it in rare cases (steps 8-9). ריש לקיש holds that משיכה comes from the Torah, so for him money never buys by Torah law. That means רב נחמן's explanation cannot work for ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: They cannot be used to make a trade-acquisition (חליפין)

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב נַחְמָן,
phrases.english: But if he holds like רב נחמן,
who says: produce does not make חליפין
and a coin does not acquire,
how does he explain it (the משנה)?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided question set up in step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: Explaining the משנה according to ריש לקיש if he follows רב נחמן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב נחמן's explanation depends on money acquiring by Torah law. ריש לקיש holds that only משיכה acquires by Torah law, so that explanation is unavailable to him.

steps.title: ריש לקיש must explain the משנה like רב ששת
steps.stepSummary: The answer: no matter what, ריש לקיש has to explain the משנה the way רב ששת does.
steps.simpleTranslation: You are forced to say that he explains it like רב ששת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 11. Whatever ריש לקיש holds, he must explain the משנה like רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's explanation depends on money acquiring by Torah law, so it cannot work for ריש לקיש. That leaves only רב ששת's explanation: the משנה's 'כיצד' shows that goods make חליפין (step 4).

keyTerms.meaning: You are forced to say; there is no other choice

phrases.aramaic: עַל כֻּרְחָךְ כְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת מְתָרֵץ לַהּ.
phrases.english: You are forced to say he explains it like רב ששת.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל כֻּרְחָךְ כְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת מְתָרֵץ לַהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Forced reading: only one explanation remains possible
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש might be able to use רב נחמן's explanation
steps.terutzMaskana: ריש לקיש must explain the משנה like רב ששת, reading 'כיצד' as showing that goods make חליפין

steps.title: ריש לקיש himself said a pouch of coins can be traded for a pouch of coins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule that a coin is not part of חליפין. ריש לקיש said that even a pouch of coins traded for another pouch of coins makes an acquisition.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: all movable items acquire one another. And ריש לקיש said: this includes even a pouch full of coins traded for a pouch full of coins!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge. It quotes ריש לקיש's comment on a משנה, which seems to say that coins can be acquired through חליפין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא's reading in step 1 leaves coins out of חליפין, because a coin is not 'appraised against another item.' But ריש לקיש says two pouches of coins acquire each other through a trade. That makes it look as though coins can be acquired through חליפין.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think ריש לקיש is saying money buys things. The question is whether coins can be the items being traded in חליפין, and he seems to say yes.

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: כׇּל הַמִּטַּלְטְלִין קוֹנִין זֶה אֶת זֶה.
phrases.english: We learned: all movable items acquire one another.
And ריש לקיש said:
even a pouch full of coins
traded for a pouch full of coins!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: כׇּל הַמִּטַּלְטְלִין קוֹנִין זֶה אֶת זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge, from ריש לקיש's own words, to the rule that a coin cannot be acquired through חליפין
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a coin is not part of חליפין and cannot be acquired through it (the reading of the משנה in step 1)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ריש לקיש says a pouch of coins traded for a pouch of coins is acquired, which means coins can be acquired through חליפין

steps.title: רב אחא: he meant coins that are no longer valid money
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא explains that ריש לקיש meant coins that have been taken out of use, either by the government or by the people of a province.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא explained it as talking about a דינר אנקא and a דינר אניגרא: one is a coin the government made invalid, and one is a coin the people of a province made invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 13. ריש לקיש was talking about coins that are no longer real money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A coin that is no longer used as money counts as an ordinary object. So it can be acquired through חליפין like any other movable item. That means ריש לקיש's statement does not contradict the rule that real coins cannot be acquired through חליפין.

keyTerms.meaning: The government made it invalid (banned the coin)
The people of a province made it invalid (stopped using it)

phrases.english: רב אחא explained it:
with an anka dinar and an anigera dinar,
phrases.notes: These are names of two types of coins. The letter in square brackets is the corrected spelling.

phrases.english: one that the government made invalid,
and one that the province made invalid.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the coins are invalid coins
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ריש לקיש meant real, valid coins, so coins can be acquired through חליפין
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant invalid coins, which count as ordinary objects, so real coins still cannot be acquired through חליפין

steps.title: Why the government-banned coin alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why both kinds of invalid coins need to be mentioned. If only the government-banned coin were taught, we might think a coin the province stopped using still counts as money.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both cases are needed. If we were taught only about a coin the government banned, I would say that is because it cannot be used at all. But a coin a province stopped using can still be spent in another province, so I would say it is still a coin, and a coin cannot be acquired through חליפין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: why mention two kinds of invalid coins? It starts with the first side of the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A coin banned by the government cannot be used anywhere, so it is clearly no longer money. A coin dropped by one province is still spent in other places, so we might think it still counts as money. Teaching that case shows that even it counts as an ordinary object for חליפין.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is necessary (to teach both cases)
For if it had taught us
I would say it is still

phrases.english: And it is necessary (to teach both),
for if it had taught us only about one the government banned,
[I would say that is] because it does not circulate at all.
But one the province stopped using,
which still circulates in another province,
I would say it is still a coin
and a coin cannot be acquired through חליפין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רב אחא's answer lists two kinds of invalid coins
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why are both types of invalid coins needed?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The government-banned case alone would not teach us about a coin still used in other provinces

steps.title: Why the province-dropped coin alone would not be enough, so both are needed
steps.stepSummary: The other side: if only the province case were taught, we might think a government-banned coin still counts as money because people use it privately. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we were taught only about a coin a province stopped using, I would say that is because it is not used there privately or publicly. But a coin the government banned can still be used privately, so I would say it is still a coin, and a coin cannot be acquired through חליפין. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why both cases are needed. Each case has a reason it might still count as money, so the teaching must cover both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the province that dropped it, nobody uses that coin at all, so it is clearly not money there. A government-banned coin may still be passed around quietly, so we might think it still counts as money. Each case has its own weak point, so both cases must be taught.
steps.whatToRemember: Real coins cannot be acquired through חליפין. When ריש לקיש said two pouches of coins can be traded, he meant coins that are no longer used as money, and both kinds of invalid coins had to be mentioned.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only about one the province stopped using,
[I would say that is] because it does not circulate
neither in private nor in public.
But one the government banned,
which still circulates in private,
I would say it is still a coin,
and a coin cannot be acquired through חליפין.
So both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second side of the explanation begun in step 15
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both kinds of invalid coins count as ordinary objects for חליפין, and each case had to be taught because each has its own reason to seem like money

steps.title: Selling for 'these coins' completes the sale
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes רב הונא: if someone says 'Sell me your item for these coins,' the buyer acquires the item.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said in the name of רב הונא: If someone says, 'Sell me your item for these coins,' he acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with a ruling from רבה in the name of רב הונא. A buyer who says 'sell me for these coins' acquires the item, and this sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyer points to specific coins, 'these,' instead of naming a price. רב הונא rules that the sale still takes effect, so neither side can back out. The new point is that a sale does not need an exact price as long as the payment is clearly identified.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who reports this ruling from his teacher
The אמורא whose ruling רבה is quoting
For these, pointing to specific coins
He acquired it, so the sale is complete

phrases.english: Rabba said that Rav Huna said:
"Sell me [your item] for these [coins]": he acquired it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The earlier discussion about banned coins has ended. This step opens a new teaching about a sale paid with coins whose amount was never stated.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a buyer says 'Sell me for these coins,' the buyer acquires the item, and the sale is complete.
